2. Electric Current (I) & Drift Dynamics
Explanation & Microscopic Concept: Electric current is defined as the net rate of flow of electric charge across a
cross-section of a conductor per unit time.
In a metallic conductor, free electrons collide continuously with vibrating lattice ions. In the absence of an external
electric field, their net directional movement is zero. When a potential difference V is applied across length L, an
electric field E = V / L accelerates electrons, imparting an average directional Drift Velocity (vd) given by vd = (e E
τ) / m (where τ is relaxation time).

Question: How much energy is given to each coulomb of charge passing through a 6 V battery?
